newsitem.title: USA: Brent sellers test waters of U.S. Gulf Coast.
newsitem.headline: Brent sellers test waters of U.S. Gulf Coast.

text.p: Several companies tested the waters of the U.S. Gulf Coast on Wednesday for possible transatlantic crude sales, traders said.
A major trading house now has four Brent cargoes and is looking to work a VLCC to the Gulf Coast, traders said.

The spread between West Texas Intermediate/Cushing and Brent for April was around $1.65-70 on Wednesday afternoon, a level which began to spark interest among various trading houses and North Sea producers.
Brent was heard offered around April WTI minus 25-35 cents for early April arrival. A cargo loading around March 10-14 would notionally go for a discount of around 15-20 cents a barrel, traders said.
On the demand side, however, many Gulf Coast refiners are already covered for several weeks.
Domestic alternatives such as Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James and Latin American crudes such as Colombian Cusiana satisfied refiners' appetites while the transatlantic window was firmly closed.
In Latin America, Colombia's state-owned Ecopetrol sold a Cusiana cargo for loading March 25-26 for around May WTI/Cushing minus 22 cents a barrel, traders said.
The unconfirmed buyer was state-owned Petroleos de Venezuela subsidiary Maraven, which was heard to be taking on foreign light barrels to offset sales of its own Mesa crude.
Venezuelan Mesa was last heard done at a discount of around $2.90 a barrel.
Meanwhile, Ecopetrol is courting a select group of refiners for Vasconia and Cano Limon cargoes, with flexible loading dates, traders said.
Elsewhere, Uruguay's state-owned oil refiner ANCAP is likely to launch a new products tender, possibly next week.
The tender would cover the country's needs until the 34,600 barrels per day (bpd) La Teja refinery resumes operations in April.
The facility was supposed to have re-started this month, but ANCAP ran into delays in replacing the catalytic cracker.
